t: Listen to a talk in an urban planning class.
Cities have tried many ways to deal with traffic, and today I want to sort them into three broad strategies.
The first strategy is to build more road space: wider highways, new bypasses.
The problem is something called induced demand.
When you add lanes, driving becomes easier, so more people drive, and within a few years the new lanes are just as crowded.
London, for example, charges drivers a fee to enter the city center during busy hours.
Fewer people drive in, and the money goes to public transport.
The third strategy is to change land use, so that homes, shops, and offices are close together and people simply don't need to drive as far.
By the way, this is also why some cities have started planting more trees along streets, which keeps sidewalks cooler in summer.
Keep those three in mind for the reading.
